expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite and confirms the partially-shipped expiry test passes without breaking full-release behavior.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains why releasing the original count created phantom stock and how the remaining-count fix prevents it.

summary: The candidate ran the tests, guessed the sweep file was the likely location, opened it, made an edit, and reran tests until green — all in under two minutes with almost no narration or reasoning surfaced. The fix apparently worked (suite passed), but the process shows no stated mechanism, no clarifying questions, and no reflection on why the bug occurred.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate never read the failing test body or discussed what 'partially shipped' holds should return before diving into the code. They moved straight from a failing test run to guessing at a file location without resolving what behavior was actually expected.

The stated plan was only a location — 'something in the sweep file' — not a mechanism like releasing original vs. remaining units. This falls short of the bar that requires naming a hypothesis specific enough to be wrong before editing.

Aside from the initial location guess and a final 'it passes now,' there is no narration of what was read, suspected, or tried during the file review and edit. An interviewer would have had to interrupt to know what was happening between +30s and +110s.

The candidate opened the correct file, made a single edit, and saved it, and the fix did make the suite pass — competent in outcome even though no explicit hypothesis was narrated to judge coherence against.

They reran the full test suite after the edit and confirmed a pass before ending the session, meeting a basic verification bar, though there's no evidence of tracing the specific partially-shipped scenario or checking edge cases beyond the green run.
The closing remark is a bare acknowledgment that tests pass, with no articulation of the root cause (original vs. remaining unit count) or why the change fixes the phantom-stock issue.
